title: Reconcile the legacy benchmarks.yml workflow against the EPIC-17 four-tier structure
summary: Audit .github/workflows/benchmarks.yml against Tier 0-3 (BM-20/21/22); either retire it, or re-scope it with a documented, non-overlapping trigger so it stops duplicating benchmark-scale.yml's weekly Sunday 04:00 UTC slot and the per-push-to-main Db2 cost.
description:
`.github/workflows/benchmarks.yml` predates EPIC-17's tiering: it runs the full pytest-benchmark suite against a live Db2 container on every push to `main`, weekly (`0 4 * * 0`), and via manual dispatch, then publishes its own HTML report + SVG histograms to gh-pages. `benchmark-scale.yml` (BM-22, EPIC-17 Tier 3) is independently scheduled for the identical weekly slot (`0 4 * * 0`) and publishes its own gh-pages content. Neither workflow's comments reference the other; there is no documented reason two separate weekly full-suite-against-live-Db2 jobs should coexist.

Determine which parts of `benchmarks.yml`'s coverage (e.g. the BM-11 adapter-overhead benchmarks it explicitly installs extras for) are and are not already exercised by Tier 1/2/3 (BM-20/21/22). If fully subsumed, retire `benchmarks.yml` and its gh-pages report tree (documenting the retirement in DECISIONS.md per this project's standing discipline of never silently deleting a benchmark artifact without a record). If it covers something the tiered workflows don't, re-scope its trigger so it no longer collides with `benchmark-scale.yml`'s schedule or duplicates the push-to-main Db2 run, and document in `benchmarks/README.md`'s workflow table (see WF-3) exactly what unique coverage justifies keeping it.

Acceptance: no two benchmark workflows share an unexplained overlapping trigger/schedule; if `benchmarks.yml` is retired, its removal and rationale are recorded in DECISIONS.md; if kept, its unique purpose is documented and cross-referenced from WF-3's workflow map.
